title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Preregistered, Artifact-Backed Evaluation of Input-Sanitization and Deterministic Verification Against Adversarial Intents
abstract: We report a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) that measured whether template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating (with at-most-one automated repair) changes the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations under adversarially mutated intents. The frozen run used the declared generator gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 within a hosted generate–validate–repair adapter. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; complete paired outcomes used in the primary analysis = 141. Observed per-pair acceptance: Baseline 135/141 (95.7447%); Guarded 141/141 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.04255319148936165; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. We reconcile preregistration language vs the formal estimand, document per-condition pipeline semantics and shared-initial-generation use, disclose the protocol deviation (unset runtime sampling temperature), and discuss operational interpretation and limitations (synthetic scope, single model/validator). All principal numeric claims are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts.

sections.introduction:
Generative LLMs are increasingly proposed to translate high-level operator intent into device CLI, promising automation gains for NetOps. But produced outputs may violate sequencing constraints, CLI grammar, or safety invariants; adversarially crafted inputs can exacerbate these risks. Prior prototypes show that coupling LLM generation with deterministic verification and localized repair reduces observable errors, yet many published evaluations rely on token- or reference-match metrics that do not directly measure deployability or acceptance by a deterministic validator [3,8,9].

This paper addresses a narrowly scoped, operational question suitable for a preregistered confirmatory test: How effective are template-based input sanitization and deterministic verifier-gating (with at-most-one automated repair) at changing the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations when inputs are adversarially mutated? The preregistered formal estimand is the paired difference in validator-accepted outcomes (guarded minus baseline) evaluated under shared_initial_candidate generation semantics, so the paired comparison isolates post-generation pipeline effects (sanitization, gating, and bounded repair) applied to the same initial LLM draft per intent.

Contributions. (1) A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment executed end-to-end with traceable analysis; (2) a precise, artifact-grounded description of per-condition pipeline semantics that enforces shared-initial-generation; (3) a confirmatory statistical result showing a small but statistically detectable absolute change in validator acceptance under the guarded pipeline on a synthetic adversarial-intent bank; and (4) explicit reconciliation of preregistration wording with the registered estimand and disclosure of a protocol deviation together with reproducibility guidance.
sections.related_work:
Deterministic verification tools such as Header Space Analysis and VeriFlow provide semantics-focused checks (reachability, isolation, rule precedence) and are widely used as pre-deployment gates in network-management workflows [5–7]. Their representational strengths make them attractive validators for LLM-generated configurations, but they require explicit formalization of invariants and do not cover every runtime or protocol-level property; prior literature therefore treats them as precise but partial oracles [5–7,14].

Empirical studies of LLM-assisted configuration (e.g., NetConfEval, NetLLMBench) report that model-only generation yields syntactic errors and higher-level sequencing or protected-interface violations; many evaluations use surface-oriented metrics that correlate poorly with deployability [3,8,9]. Generate–validate–repair architectures and tool-assisted orchestration (including Toolformer-style approaches) show promise: external checks integrated into generation loops can improve concrete outcomes provided verifier diagnostics are actionable and repair scope is bounded [11,3]. Security analyses document prompt-injection and indirect-prompt attacks against LLM-integrated systems, motivating sanitization, slot-validation, and gating defenses; however, NetOps-specific threat-modeling and rigorous mitigation evaluations are still limited [10].

This study situates itself against this body of work by preregistering an estimand that uses deterministic-validator acceptance as the primary quantity of interest and by enforcing shared_initial_candidate semantics so that post-generation safeguards are the causal interventions under test.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study cand-2026-03 was preregistered before observing outcomes. The primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) defines, for each adversarial intent, a binary outcome equal to 1 if the deterministic validator would accept the final candidate for deployment and 0 otherwise. The confirmatory test is an exact two-sided McNemar; bootstrap percentile 95% CIs used 10,000 resamples with seed = 1729.

Design, task bank and adversary model. The preregistered design targeted N = 150 adversarial intents. Synthetic intent templates exercise interface admin changes, MTU and VLAN updates, and required sequencing patterns (e.g., shutdown–change–restore). The adversary applied deterministic mutation heuristics to these templates; generation seeds and mutation taxonomy are archived. Scope is expressly limited to the synthetic templates and deterministic CLI grammar used; no private production data were used.

Model, validator and orchestration. The declared generator was gpt-5-mini and the deterministic validator was deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Orchestration implemented a generate–validate–repair workflow with two per-pair conditions: Baseline (validator applied directly to the shared initial candidate) and Guarded (template-based input-sanitizer applied prior to gating; policy permitted at most one automated repair LLM call per pair). The registered generation semantics were shared_initial_candidate: a single LLM call produced the draft reused by both conditions for each intent, so any observed paired difference arises solely from downstream sanitization/gating/repair steps.

Missingness and planned benign control. The preregistered missingness rule excluded a paired unit only when both paired runs were technical failures (model API failure, verifier timeout, or parser error). The preregistration also specified a benign-control (M = 50) to measure false-positive blocking; this benign-control was not executed in the archived run and therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking rates are reported. This omission is reported here explicitly and constrains interpretation of false-positive risk.
sections.results:
Execution and counts. The archived execution completed 282 of the planned 300 episodes; 18 episodes failed for technical reasons and were handled per the preregistered missingness rule. After applying the preregistered exclusion (exclude pair only when both paired runs were technical failures), 141 complete pairs entered the primary analysis. Provider-call accounting documented 156 hosted-model-call events (147 completed, 9 failed) and stage counts indicating 150 shared initial generations and 6 repair-stage calls.

Condition-level outcomes and paired inference. Condition summary: Baseline accepted = 135 of 141 complete pairs (baseline success rate = 0.9574468085106383); Guarded accepted = 141 of 141 (guarded success rate = 1.0). The paired contingency counts were n11 = 135 (both accepted), n10 = 6 (guarded accepted, baseline rejected), n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar test on these paired outcomes yields p = 0.03125. Observed paired point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165. The 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) is [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. All numerical results reported above are reproduced by the archived analysis artifacts.

Discordant-case diagnostics and repairs. The six discordant n10 pairs are associated with the guarded pipeline enabling acceptance after sanitizer normalization or a single permitted automated repair (repair-stage calls = 6). In each discordant pair the shared_initial_candidate was identical between Baseline and Guarded (the same initial draft per the shared-initial design); the Guarded pipeline converted an initially rejected draft into a validator-accepted candidate via sanitizer normalization or the one allowed repair. These diagnostics show that the guarded pipeline increased validator acceptance by recovering reparable drafts rather than by simply rejecting more candidates.

Missingness sensitivity. Nine paired units were excluded because both runs failed technically. A conservative sensitivity calculation that treats those excluded pairs as failures yields baseline acceptance = 135/150 = 0.9000 and guarded acceptance = 141/150 = 0.9400; this demonstrates that technical failures reduce effective sample size but do not invert the observed paired difference under conservative assumptions.

Unexecuted preregistered items. The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and its false-positive-blocking estimand were not executed; consequently no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made. This absence is disclosed here and constrains interpretations that would have required those results.
sections.discussion:
Reconciliation of preregistered language and formal estimand. The preregistration's natural-language H1 suggested that verifier-gating would reduce attacker success (fewer unsafe configurations accepted). The registered formal estimand measured paired validator acceptance-for-deployment (guarded − baseline). Our observed guarded > baseline difference (~4.255 percentage points) reflects the Guarded pipeline recovering initial drafts to validator-accepted candidates via sanitizer normalization or bounded repair. Therefore the formal-estimand improvement does not by itself prove reduced attacker success under an attacker-centric definition; it demonstrates that guarded post-generation processing increases the validator-accepted yield by enabling reparable drafts to pass the validator.

Operational implications. In synthetic settings, input sanitization combined with bounded automated repair can reduce operator rework by converting invalid drafts into validator-accepted candidates. That operational benefit presumes repairs preserve intended semantics; repairs that mask adversarial manipulations could increase risk. This trade-off motivates co-design: gating policies, repair scope, and validator expressiveness must be jointly specified to maintain safety in deployment.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: 18 technical failures reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion was preregistered and applied. Construct validity: the deterministic validator encodes CLI grammar, sequencing and protected-interface invariants but does not capture all dynamic protocol-level semantics; validator acceptance is therefore a partial proxy for operational safety. External validity: single generator (gpt-5-mini), single validator, and synthetic intent bank limit generalization across vendors, CLI dialects, and production settings. Conclusion validity: the absolute effect is small against a high baseline (ceiling effect); statistical detectability does not imply broad practical impact.

Reproducibility, protocol deviation and recommendations. The archived run recorded an unset runtime sampling temperature (temperature field unset), a protocol deviation we disclose because provider defaults can affect sampling. To preserve paired comparability the pipeline enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics (single generation per pair) and the provider-call accounting confirms the realized call pattern. For deterministic reproduction we recommend explicitly setting sampling parameters (e.g., temperature = 0) and re-executing with the archived task bank. Recommended next steps: run the preregistered benign-control to estimate false-positive blocking; preregister an attacker-centric estimand coupling validator acceptance with an independent semantic-safety oracle; diversify generators and validators across vendors and CLI dialects; and fix sampling settings for deterministic reproduction.
sections.conclusion: A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment on a synthetic adversarial intent bank found that template-based input sanitization with deterministic verifier-gating and at-most-one automated repair produced a small but statistically detectable absolute increase in deterministic-validator-accepted LLM-generated configurations under the archived formal estimand (paired difference ≈ 0.04255; p = 0.03125; 95% CI [0.01418, 0.07801]). Diagnostics indicate the six discordant pairs were associated with permitted repair or sanitizer normalization that enabled acceptance. Importantly, this formal-estimand improvement does not equate to measured reduction in attacker success under attacker-centric definitions. The run is limited by synthetic scope, a single model and validator, and a protocol deviation (unset sampling temperature). Future work should execute the preregistered benign-control, measure attacker-centric estimands with an independent semantic-safety oracle, diversify models and validators, and fix explicit sampling parameters for reproducible deterministic runs. All principal numbers above are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts available in the study's artifact bundle.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock under the archived master prompt (provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human role and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock; all literature review, preregistration, study selection, code generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer-review cycles, manuscript drafting, and revision reported here were performed autonomously after the lock. Declared models/tools and orchestration: primary generator = gpt-5-mini, deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5, orchestration adapter = hosted generate–validate–repair adapter. Preregistration: study cand-2026-03 was preregistered prior to observing outcomes. Protocol deviation: the archived run recorded an unset runtime sampling temperature (provider-side default); this is disclosed because sampling defaults can affect reproduction. To preserve paired comparability the pipeline enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics (single shared generation per pair). Archived execution and analysis artifacts (execution and analysis manifests, scoring summaries, and reconciliation logs) document the numeric claims and diagnostic traces; the full artifact bundle is available with the paper's supplementary materials. No human manually edited or corrected manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to deterministic mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated.
A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; results are reported and interpreted with respect to the archived formal estimand.
The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
